source.title: SGD Generalizes Better Than GD (And Regularization Doesn't Help)
source.authors: I Zaghloul Amir; Tomer Koren; Roi Livni

record.tranche_reason: The paper gives theoretical results for stochastic convex optimization, but does not test the natural-label neural-network claim or any listed version. Its discussion connects the results to generalization in practice without testing that claim.
record.gate_note: The paper proves lower bounds for GD on constructed convex optimization problems. It mentions SGD's O(1/ε²) guarantee as background and cites prior results; those are not extracted as this paper's results.
record.test_reason: The study proves worst-case lower bounds for full-batch GD on constructed stochastic convex optimization problems. It does not test any listed neural-network version. In particular, its SGD–GD separation does not compare batch sizes under fixed epoch budgets as V5 requires.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is substantially correct. The authors establish a worst-case separation between SGD and GD in stochastic convex optimization: GD requires Ω(ε⁻⁴) iterations to match SGD's known O(ε⁻²) guarantee. Regularization does not improve this requirement for the specified learning-rate schedule and averaging procedure; extending that result to arbitrary schedules and averaging remains open.
record.recipe_differences: Theoretical lower-bound constructions in stochastic convex optimization, not neural-network experiments on natural labels.
record.method_sensitivity: The bounds depend on the learning rate, iteration count, sample size, dimension, and, for regularized GD, the regularization parameter and learning-rate schedule.

fits_no_version.finding: Constructed convex problems establish a worst-case Ω(ε⁻⁴) iteration requirement for fixed-step GD, compared with the known O(ε⁻²) SGD guarantee. The analyzed regularized GD procedure retains this iteration requirement; another construction establishes susceptibility to overtraining.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In stochastic convex optimization, the optimization algorithm and training schedule affect dimension-independent excess-risk guarantees; full-batch GD can require more iterations than SGD, including with the specific regularization procedure analyzed.

record.peer_reviewed: Annual Conference on Computational Learning Theory (COLT) 2021; accepted for presentation at COLT 2021
record.problems: The evidence is theoretical and relies on constructed convex losses and dimension conditions; it does not establish results for neural networks or natural-label datasets.
record.rows_left_out: No rows omitted. The O(1/ε²) SGD guarantee is presented as background, and the cited comparison results are prior work rather than this paper's own findings.

untested.parts: Random-label memorization and natural-label held-out accuracy using the same neural-network architectures and recipes.
Test error as network width increases beyond the width needed to fit.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers and the contribution of local connectivity.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD under limited or broader tuning.
Batch-size effects on image classifiers or language models under fixed epoch budgets, including recipe adaptations.
Dropout effects on held-out classification error.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and its association with neural-network generalization gaps.
Test-accuracy effects of removing memorized training examples versus random examples.

record.verdict_notes: The rows describe legitimate theoretical results, but their states cannot establish any listed version. Iteration counts in this comparison are not fixed epoch budgets. The SGD upper guarantee is background, not a new result of this study.

versions.untested_parts: Natural-label and random-label fitting and generalization in neural networks.
Width sweeps and test error beyond the interpolation threshold.
Convolutional versus fully connected networks on image data.
Adaptive optimizers and their held-out performance under different tuning recipes.
Large-batch training and its held-out performance under fixed epoch budgets.
Sharpness measures and their association with generalization gaps.
Removing memorized examples and measuring test-accuracy changes.

rows.subject: GD on a constructed convex Lipschitz loss
rows.operation_detail: Theoretical lower bound on expected population risk of the averaged GD output.
rows.measure: Expected excess population risk, E[F(wS)] − min_w F(w)
rows.note: Existence result: for every η > 0, T ≥ 1, and n, the authors construct a convex 3-Lipschitz loss and distribution meeting the stated dimension condition.
rows.check: The bound correctly records Theorem 6.1, but measures none of V1–V8. Theorem 3.1 additionally includes an optimization-error term and requires d ≥ T·2^(n+5) + 20η²T²; distinguish these statements.

rows.subject: GD on a constructed regularized convex Lipschitz loss
rows.operation_detail: Theoretical lower bound on expected population risk for GD applied to a regularized empirical objective with the specified schedule and averaging.
rows.measure: Expected excess population risk, E[F(wS)] − F(w⋆)
rows.note: Existence result for a constructed convex 3-Lipschitz loss and distribution.
rows.check: Theorem 6.4 gives (3/4) min{1/(8λ√(T+1)), 1/16}; the record omits the factor 3/4. The condition is 0 < λ < 3. This theoretical excess-risk bound measures none of V1–V8.

rows.subject: GD on a constructed convex loss
rows.operation_detail: Theoretical lower bound on expected population risk after T iterations.
rows.measure: Expected excess population risk, E[F(wS)] − min_w F(w)
rows.note: Existence result for a constructed convex 3-Lipschitz loss and distribution; the paper says it suggests GD may overfit after enough training steps.
rows.check: Theorem 6.8 gives min{max{1/8 − 2^(2n+2)/(4ηT), 0}, 1/48}. The record incorrectly adds an outer factor 1/8, substitutes 1/4 inside, and exchanges the outer minimum for a maximum. This bound measures none of V1–V8.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
